description: <div class="content-intro"><h2>WHAT MAKES US EPIC?</h2> <p>At the core of Epic’s success are talented, passionate people. Epic prides itself on creating a collaborative, welcoming, and creative environment. Whether it’s building award-winning games or crafting engine technology that enables others to make visually stunning interactive experiences, we’re always innovating.</p> <p>Being Epic means being a part of a team that continually strives to do right by our community and users. We’re constantly innovating to raise the bar of engine and game development.</p></div><h2>PROGRAMMING - UNREAL ENGINE</h2> <h3><strong>What We Do</strong></h3> <p>Unreal-powered projects have been on the bleeding edge of real-time entertainment for over 20 years. Our team of programming experts are always innovating to improve the tools and technology that empower content developers worldwide.</p> <h3><strong>What You'll Do</strong></h3> <p>Epic Games is seeking an experienced Senior Language Programmer to join our Verse team, which owns the toolchain (compiler, VM, and runtime) that powers game development in Unreal Engine and UEFN. You'll work on the systems every UE and UEFN developer relies on to build and ship games with Verse.</p> <h3><strong>In this role, you will</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Extend, evolve, and maintain the Verse compiler toolchain, transactional memory runtime and VM, add new platform support, implement new language features and integrate with Unreal Engine's content, build, and cooking pipelines</li> <li>Optimize performance, memory usage, and iteration times across the Verse toolchain, runtime and UE/Verse boundary</li> <li>Work closely with language consumers to ensure an exceptional user experience</li> <li>Establish test workflows to validate improvements and prevent regressions</li> <li>Design and maintain the scripting interface to Unreal Engine, working in close collaboration with the Verse Language team and the broader UE engineering organization</li> </ul> <h3><strong>What we're looking for</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Expert knowledge of C++17 or later</li> <li>Experience in compiler or toolchain development (e.g., compiler internals, VM design, Clang/LLVM, or linker/platform ABI specifics)</li> <li>Experience developing and optimizing large codebases, with the ability to make tradeoffs between usability, performance, and power</li> <li>Strong ability to reason about large, interconnected systems</li> <li>Solid grounding in software engineering principles, including API design</li> <li>Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to work autonomously and deliver practical solutions</li> <li>Experience with Unreal Engine integration is a plus</li> </ul> <h2>EPIC JOB + EPIC BENEFITS = EPIC LIFE</h2> <p>Our intent is to cover all things that are medically necessary and improve the quality of life. We pay 100% of the premiums for both you and your dependents. Our coverage includes Medical, Dental, a Vision HRA, Long Term Disability, Life Insurance &amp; a 401k with competitive match. We also offer a robust mental well-being program through Modern Health, which provides free therapy and coaching for employees &amp; dependents.&nbsp;</p> <p>Throughout the year we celebrate our employees with events and company-wide paid breaks. We offer unlimited PTO and sick time and recognize individuals for 7 years of employment with a paid sabbatical.&nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp; &nbsp;</p><div class="content-conclusion"><h2>ABOUT US</h2> <p>Epic Games​ ​is a leading interactive entertainment company. For over 30 years we've been making award-winning games and engine technology that empowers others to make visually stunning games and 3D content that bring environments to life like never before. Epic's award-winning Unreal Engine technology not only provides game developers the ability to build high-fidelity, interactive experiences for PC, console, mobile, and VR, it is also a tool being embraced by content creators across a variety of industries such as media and entertainment, automotive, and architectural design. As we continue to build our Engine technology and develop remarkable games, we strive to build teams of world-class talent.</p> <h3><strong>Like what you hear? Come be a part of something Epic!</strong></h3> <p>Epic Games deeply values diverse teams and an inclusive work culture, and we are proud to be an Equal Opportunity employer. Learn more about our Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) Policy <a href="https://www.epicgames.com/site/en-US/eeo-policy" target="_blank">here</a>.</p> <p><strong>Note to Recruitment Agencies: </strong>Epic does not accept any unsolicited resumes or approaches from any unauthorized third party (including recruitment or placement agencies) (i.e., a third party with whom we do not have a negotiated and validly executed agreement). We will not pay any fees to any unauthorized third party. Further details on these matters can be found <a href="https://www.epicgames.com/note-to-recruitment-agencies" target="_blank">here</a>.</p></div> Find more English Speaking Jobs in United Kingdom on Arbeitnow

About the role

Billions have gone into enterprise AI. Most of it isn't working — organisations still can't turn model capability into measurable business impact. It's a hard, unsolved technical challenge: building the systems that translate what AI can do into how work actually gets done inside real organisations, at scale, with proof it's working. We're hiring a Senior Leader of Product Marketing, reporting to the CPTO, to own the positioning, competitive intelligence, and go-to-market orchestration that makes that story credible to buyers who've heard "AI transformation" pitches before and have learned to discount them. You'll sit at the center of Product, Engineering, Sales, B2B Marketing, CS, and executive leadership — turning hard technical work into a case buyers trust, giving Sales what they need to win the deals that matter, and grounding pricing and roadmap decisions in real market evidence.

Positioning & narrative

Market & competitive intelligence

  • Run competitive intelligence (win-loss analysis, competitor tracking, technical benchmarking) and be the most credible voice in the room on what the market actually believes — evidence, not anecdote

  • Define launch success metrics and report on them credibly to executive leadership

  • Champion and put structure around the shift toward faster product launches — building quickly and iterating based on real performance

Sales & CS enablement

  • Own strategic decisions on positioning, enablement, and the go-to-market motion for Sales leadership, not just content delivery

Team & function leadership

title: Network Operation Engineer
description: Network Operations Engineer 1. About the role Share is the global marketplace for bandwidth. We aggregate telco infrastructure into a single layer and give ISPs, hyperscalers, and AI companies a clean path to deliver connectivity into every home and business across Kenya and the continent. Behind that marketplace is a real network: a BGP edge peering with Tier 1 transit, hyperscalers, and local exchanges, an MPLS backbone, aggregation and access gear, and the systems that watch all of it. For the partners who run on us, the network is the product, and the NOC is where they feel it. A clean shift is a partner who never knew anything happened. That is the bar. We are early and the team is small, so we cannot afford a pair of hands that only knows how to escalate. We need a capable network engineer who can stand a shift, resolve real faults without waking anyone, and then keep building the network while East Africa sleeps: propagation and peering checks, health passes across the estate, config changes through to merge, tickets off the board, automation that takes the next repetitive job off everyone's plate. The watching is the floor of this role, not the ceiling. The NOC you would be joining is not a legacy one. We are building it as an AI assisted operations environment from the ground up. The forwarding plane runs on open source routing and forwarding software, every device configuration lives in Git, and an LLM layer sits on top of the live network state. When something moves, that layer reads the telemetry, correlates it against the topology and the config history, and puts a probable cause and a candidate fix in front of the engineer on shift. The point is not to replace your judgment. It is to collapse the time between an alert firing and you knowing where to look, so mean time to repair is measured in minutes. You sit inside that system. You use it, you push back on it when it is wrong, and what you catch that it misses is part of how it gets smarter. As we build automation out across the NOC, you are not just a consumer of the tooling. You help write it. 2. What you'll do Watch, and know what you're looking at. Sit on our monitoring stack (Zabbix and Grafana dashboards, flow telemetry, alerting) and actually read it. Learn what normal looks like so abnormal jumps out at you: a BGP session that dropped, a link that went down, latency climbing on a path, a capacity threshold breached, a partner suddenly pushing or pulling nothing. Troubleshoot and resolve. This is where you earn your seat. Confirm the alert is real, gather the facts, and localise the fault: one peer or many, us or upstream, a real outage or a monitoring blip. The assistive layer surfaces a likely diagnosis and a suggested fix, the config history is right there in Git, and the runbooks are live. Your job is to read all of it critically, decide what is actually true, and close out what you can on your own. Every ticket you resolve yourself is one our senior people did not get pulled out of deep work, or out of bed, to deal with. Keep the network healthy, not just alive. A quiet shift is not an idle one. Run the proactive passes: check that routes are propagating the way they should, that RPKI and filter chains are doing their job, that peering and transit sessions are clean across the edge, that no PoP is drifting toward a capacity wall. Catch the slow degradations that never trip an alert. The day team should inherit a network in a known good state. Build and automate. The repetitive parts of this job should not stay repetitive. Write the scripts that turn a manual check into a scheduled one. Push our config automation forward (Jinja driven generation, NAPALM or NETCONF/gNMI against the devices) so changes ship from data, not from memory. When the assistive layer keeps missing the same thing, that is a candidate for automation, and you are well placed to build it during the hours nobody else is online. Move the work forward. You are part of the network team, working the same board they do. Pick up tickets from the Linear queue, take config changes through review to merge, and keep our source of truth (Nautobot) accurate as the estate changes. Real work lands while East Africa is offline, so the team wakes up further ahead than they went to bed. Report exactly what is happening. raw.title: Network Operation Engineer
raw.description:
Network Operations Engineer

1. About the role

Share is the global marketplace for bandwidth. We aggregate telco infrastructure into a single layer and give ISPs, hyperscalers, and AI companies a clean path to deliver connectivity into every home and business across Kenya and the continent. Behind that marketplace is a real network: a BGP edge peering with Tier 1 transit, hyperscalers, and local exchanges, an MPLS backbone, aggregation and access gear, and the systems that watch all of it.

For the partners who run on us, the network is the product, and the NOC is where they feel it. A clean shift is a partner who never knew anything happened. That is the bar.

We are early and the team is small, so we cannot afford a pair of hands that only knows how to escalate. We need a capable network engineer who can stand a shift, resolve real faults without waking anyone, and then keep building the network while East Africa sleeps: propagation and peering checks, health passes across the estate, config changes through to merge, tickets off the board, automation that takes the next repetitive job off everyone's plate. The watching is the floor of this role, not the ceiling.

The NOC you would be joining is not a legacy one. We are building it as an AI assisted operations environment from the ground up. The forwarding plane runs on open source routing and forwarding software, every device configuration lives in Git, and an LLM layer sits on top of the live network state. When something moves, that layer reads the telemetry, correlates it against the topology and the config history, and puts a probable cause and a candidate fix in front of the engineer on shift. The point is not to replace your judgment. It is to collapse the time between an alert firing and you knowing where to look, so mean time to repair is measured in minutes.

You sit inside that system. You use it, you push back on it when it is wrong, and what you catch that it misses is part of how it gets smarter. As we build automation out across the NOC, you are not just a consumer of the tooling. You help write it.

2. What you'll do

Watch, and know what you're looking at. Sit on our monitoring stack (Zabbix and Grafana dashboards, flow telemetry, alerting) and actually read it. Learn what normal looks like so abnormal jumps out at you: a BGP session that dropped, a link that went down, latency climbing on a path, a capacity threshold breached, a partner suddenly pushing or pulling nothing.

Troubleshoot and resolve. This is where you earn your seat. Confirm the alert is real, gather the facts, and localise the fault: one peer or many, us or upstream, a real outage or a monitoring blip. The assistive layer surfaces a likely diagnosis and a suggested fix, the config history is right there in Git, and the runbooks are live. Your job is to read all of it critically, decide what is actually true, and close out what you can on your own. Every ticket you resolve yourself is one our senior people did not get pulled out of deep work, or out of bed, to deal with.

Keep the network healthy, not just alive. A quiet shift is not an idle one. Run the proactive passes: check that routes are propagating the way they should, that RPKI and filter chains are doing their job, that peering and transit sessions are clean across the edge, that no PoP is drifting toward a capacity wall. Catch the slow degradations that never trip an alert. The day team should inherit a network in a known good state.

Build and automate. The repetitive parts of this job should not stay repetitive. Write the scripts that turn a manual check into a scheduled one. Push our config automation forward (Jinja driven generation, NAPALM or NETCONF/gNMI against the devices) so changes ship from data, not from memory. When the assistive layer keeps missing the same thing, that is a candidate for automation, and you are well placed to build it during the hours nobody else is online.

Move the work forward. You are part of the network team, working the same board they do. Pick up tickets from the Linear queue, take config changes through review to merge, and keep our source of truth (Nautobot) accurate as the estate changes. Real work lands while East Africa is offline, so the team wakes up further ahead than they went to bed.

Report exactly what is happening. For everything you cannot or should not fix alone, the handoff has to be clean: what is wrong, where, since when, what is affected, whether it is getting worse, and what you have already tried. No guessing dressed up as fact. No "the internet is down." A clear, written incident note a senior engineer can act on the moment they open it, and a tidy handover to the East Africa team at the end of your shift.

Escalate well. Know the ladder cold: what you are cleared to touch, what you must not touch alone, and who to bring in for what. Escalating early on a genuine outage is good judgment. Sitting silently on a problem because you were unsure is the one thing that gets people out of bed angry. Handle what you can, raise the rest fast and clearly, and do not turn either dial too far.

3. Who we're looking for

A network engineer who can stand on their own through a shift, and who treats the quiet hours as time to build rather than time to wait. You will not be the most senior engineer on this team, and you do not need to be. The people you escalate to are CCIE level. What we need from you is independence and range: work a problem properly, resolve a fair share of it yourself, and use what is left of the shift to actually move the network forward. Pair that with clear reporting, sound judgment about when to bring in help, and the instinct to question a machine's suggestion rather than follow it blindly, and you are who we are looking for.

Must-have

  • Strong networking competence, held in your hands rather than on paper. CCNA and well beyond it. You understand TCP/IP, routing and switching, IP addressing and subnetting, DNS, DHCP, NAT, and how they behave when they go wrong.

  • Real troubleshooting instinct. Given a degraded link or a dropped session, you know where to look and what to rule out. You can read BGP session state, follow a path with ping and traceroute, and tell a local fault from an upstream one without waiting to be told.

  • Working BGP knowledge. Reading communities and route policy, spotting a flap or a leaky origin, understanding how transit, peering, and RPKI behave at the edge.

  • Comfortable on the gear and the CLI. Linux, network device CLIs, and dashboards are familiar ground. We run MikroTik (RouterOS) across the network and so do many partners, so RouterOS experience is a real plus.

  • Comfortable working with config in Git. Configuration lives in repos, not on devices. Reading a diff, understanding why a config changed, and proposing one yourself should not be foreign to you.

  • Some scripting, and the appetite to do more. Bash or Python, enough to automate the repetitive parts away and to grow into our config and automation pipelines. We are not hiring a button pusher.

  • Clear written English. You can describe a technical situation accurately and briefly so someone picking it up cold understands it instantly.

  • Calm under pressure and dependable. When the graphs go red you get more precise, not more panicked. You show up for every shift, alert and on time.

  • Located in New Zealand or a nearby time zone where covering our deep overnight maps onto your normal working day.

Nice-to-have

  • CCNP, or MikroTik MTCNA / MTCRE.

  • IPv6 and dual stack exposure, and internet exchange operations (looking glass and route server behaviour, IRR and RPKI hygiene).

4. What we offer

  • A seat inside a serious, very senior network team, with people who have deep service provider backgrounds and will sharpen you fast. You will see how a real carrier network behaves under live conditions.

  • A front row seat to how a network actually gets run in 2026. Open source forwarding, config as code, and an LLM layer doing real operational work. Not a slide about the future of network operations, but the environment you would work in every shift, and help build.

title: Golang Backend Engineer, Financial Product Fraud
description: Our Global Structure Deliveroo is now part of DoorDash, bringing together teams with even greater reach, scale, and ambition. Depending on your role, you may collaborate with teammates, systems, and leaders across DoorDash and Wolt. Together, we're unlocking new possibilities as one global team. Your job is to make sure every payout and transaction lands with the right person. We have spent years getting very good at protecting the things a marketplace has always had to protect: checkout fraud, account takeover, courier abuse. But we are no longer only a marketplace. We now issue banking products, lend to merchants, move instant payouts to couriers, and collect cash on the doorstep. Every one of those is a new way for money to leave the platform. This is a new team, and it owns that surface: fraud wherever money moves through the platform. Who receives it, who lends it, who collects it, and who holds it in a financial account. Think instant payout rails, merchant cash advances, and platform-issued banking and earned-wage products serving millions of couriers and merchants. These are live loss surfaces, and the volume grows with every financial product we launch. We are now looking for a Backend Engineer (Golang) to build that protection. You will design and ship real-time detection and automated enforcement for our financial products across DoorDash, Wolt, and Deliveroo. The work is high-throughput, low-latency, and unusually consequential: a rule you ship on Monday can stop a serious loss by Friday. It is also close to greenfield, so you will be setting the patterns every future financial product inherits on day one. This role will be based in London , UK as one of the founding engineering roles in our London hub, working closely with our teams in Helsinki and Berlin. What you'll do: Build and maintain high-throughput, low-latency backend services in Go that score financial events in real time, including payout enrollments, bank account links, credit applications, and account-to-account transfers. Design fraud detection and automated enforcement for our financial products end to end: from signal collection through to the decision that blocks a fraudulent payout. Build on and extend our shared fraud decisioning platform, so signals, rules, and models work across all three of our brands instead of being rebuilt three times. Partner closely with risk analysts, data scientists, and product managers to turn observed fraud patterns into shipped detection, and to know when a rule, a model, or a product change is the right answer. Work across team boundaries with our account security, payments fraud, and financial product teams. We build on their signals rather than rebuild them, so clean interfaces matter. Contribute to architectural discussions and technical decisions as we establish the fraud infrastructure baseline for financial products, with support from senior engineers on the team. Write well-tested, observable code and help the team hold a high quality bar. In fraud, a silent failure is a loss event. Our expectations: 3 to 6 years of professional software engineering experience, including backend services you have shipped and owned in production. 1+ years of production experience in Golang, or strong experience in another backend language and real enthusiasm for picking Go up quickly. A working understanding of low-latency, high-throughput distributed systems. Real-time decisioning comes with a latency budget, and you are keen to learn to build inside one. Hands-on experience with SQL and/or NoSQL databases, and some exposure to event-driven architectures (Kafka or similar). Willingness to operate what you build, including a share of on-call, with a pragmatic approach to reliability. Uses AI tooling in day-to-day development and can critically evaluate its output for correctness and quality. Nice to have Experience in fraud, risk, payments, lending, or financial crime, especially money movement fraud, bank account linking fraud, payout abuse, or lending fraud. Experience with rules engines, real-time feature stores, or ML model serving in a decisioning path. Background in Kotlin, Java, Python, or Node.js alongside Go. Familiarity with cloud infrastructure (AWS, GCP). Experience working across multiple brands, regions, or regulatory regimes. What we value A product-oriented mindset. You think beyond the ticket, understand the "why" behind the work, and take a high level of responsibility for outcomes rather than output. Comfort with ambiguity. This is a new team on a new surface; parts of the charter are still being drawn, and you will help draw them. A track record of owning a project or feature end to end, especially in fast-paced environments. Clear and proactive communication, with a collaborative spirit. We work across three companies and several time zones, so we move fast, but we succeed together. An adversarial instinct. The best fraud engineers enjoy thinking like the attacker. Diversity, Equity and Inclusion At Deliveroo, we know that a great workplace reflects the world around us and that true diversity and inclusion make us stronger, more creative, and better at what we do. We're committed to fostering an environment where everyone can do their best work and feel they belong. We believe in equality of opportunity and welcome candidates from all backgrounds regardless of age, gender, ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity, socio-economic background, religion, or belief. If you have a disability or long-term health condition and need support to apply for one of our roles, or require any reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process, you'll have the opportunity to let us know once you've submitted your application. We'll share details on how to request support so we can ensure you have a fair and equitable experience. If you're excited about making a real impact in a fast-moving marketplace and growing your career alongside ambitious, supportive teams, we'd love to hear from you!   • Competitive salary and benefits package

  • A culture of growth and development, with opportunities to expand your expertise in AI, cybersecurity, and engineering

Founded in 2016, we are a remote-first team of over 1,000 people building a top Y-Combinator company and have been profitable since 2022. We’re the leader in Long-Term Care staffing and are rapidly expanding into Home Health, Hospitals, and more, meaning we have more work to do than people to do it, and are growing our team to support millions more people and their communities.

 

Overview

The Operations Strategy Associate role is a generalist role at Clipboard suited for the “all-around athlete” type who wants exposure to a range of problems and opportunities.

You’re likely someone who’s interested in and capable of solving different problem types, you’re resourceful, adaptable, and confident you can figure it out if you can sink your teeth in deep enough. These are the ingredients for a problem-solver who is eager to flex into multiple different types of roles and responsibilities depending on what’s needed and most impactful.

While we know that you'll likely start working within one of our Operations teams, we don’t know exactly what work or projects you’ll drive out of the gate, so you’ll notice the work we’re advertising isn’t entirely specific. Some candidates may begin in more execution-focused roles within Operations, depending on their strengths, while others may take on project or team leadership earlier on.

But we’ll make a few promises about the role: it will be high-impact, fast-paced work that directly affects our customers, product, and business.

 

What you’ll Be Doing

  • Analyze operational data to spot trends and bottlenecks, and build dashboards, reports, and models that guide business decisions.

  • Research, evaluate, and implement new technologies, including AI, automations, and internal tools, to make operations more effective.

  • Design processes, workflows, and operating procedures that improve efficiency, quality, and customer experience

  • Lead cross-functional projects and strategic initiatives from planning through execution, partnering with Operations, Product, Engineering, Customer Success, and other teams.

Here are a few projects you might own:

  • Redesign how we reach out to workplaces about switching payment methods, such as moving check-paying customers to eCheck, to speed up cash collection.

  • Research, vet, and onboard a vendor that brings AI agents into our customer-facing operations.

  • Build a predictive model that flags high-risk payers early and accurately, so we can act before payments go overdue.

  • Take over a team of agents within one of our Operations teams and improve its performance, quality, and workflows.

 

What you’ll Need

  • 2+ years of work or internship experience, including but not limited to cross-functional roles such as Strategy/Business/Product Operations, Program Management, Consultancy or Business Analytics.

  • Experience solving operational problems by improving processes, designing workflows, or building scalable systems, while juggling multiple priorities in ambiguous, fast-moving environments.

  • Strong data analysis skills with hands-on experience in SQL, Python, or similar tools.

  • Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to explain complex problems simply and align stakeholders across teams.

  • A deep curiosity that drives you to reason from first principles and dig until you find the root cause.

We are hiring for multiple openings in this role and won’t close the funnel prematurely based on other candidates, but may periodically pause applications due to volume. We hope to welcome everyone who meets our bar for excellence, and we hope that includes you.

  • Fast-paced startup environment. Join a company that values curiosity, independence, and growth.

  • A hiring process that rewards skills, not just experience. Every applicant gets a fair shot, our selection is based on real-world problem-solving ability, not just credentials.

  • Opportunity to make a significant impact with our customers on both sides of the marketplace.

     

Hiring Process

  2. Case Study

  4. Interview with our Head of Operations

The scope goes beyond integrating with APIs. You’ll build ways to ingest unstructured policy updates, regulatory guidance and published documents, turning them into reliable data our intelligence layer can use.

The role is open across the European countries where we currently employ or engage remote engineers. Our backend is built primarily in Python and Django, with Django REST Framework and FastAPI supporting APIs in a service-oriented architecture deployed on AWS and Kubernetes. PostgreSQL, Redis, and Celery underpin data-intensive and asynchronous workflows. AI-assisted, spec-driven development is part of normal engineering practice at Plentific. Track record of designing and safely evolving complex relational data models in a large, long-lived production codebase, using ERDs and written technical designs to align engineers and stakeholders while preserving design quality, testability, maintainability, and safe evolution. Plentific's agentic software development transformation is already under way and producing results. Success looks like a team that is continuously getting stronger: accelerating delivery cadence against business commitments, rising engineering standards, and an agentic development practice that compounds month on month.

Engineering Leadership

The Staff Engineer, AI / ML — Self-Serve Toolchain will build the end-to-end system that lets customers adapt UFORCE models on their own private data without exposing that data to us.

This role spans data processing, foundation-model-assisted labeling, human-in-the-loop QA, active learning, training, evaluation, and model promotion. You will turn an in-flight principal-led capability into a repeatable toolchain that non-expert customers can run safely on-site.

What you’ll do

 

  • Own the ML adaptation pipeline from raw customer data to trained, evaluated, deployable models.

  • Build foundation-model-assisted labeling workflows using tools such as SAM-2, Grounding DINO, open-vocabulary models, LLM steering, and human review.

  • Design self-serve operator workflows using yes/no/maybe feedback and natural-language corrections.

  • Create versioned datasets with lineage, data cards, label provenance, class distributions, and known gaps.

  • Build QA methods that catch systematic pseudo-label errors, missing annotations, and long-tail data gaps.

  • Develop active-learning loops that prioritize the highest-value frames for limited operator review.

  • Build reproducible train/eval pipelines with experiment tracking, model packaging, and promotion gates.

  • Design evaluation around held-out anchor sets, leakage prevention, baselines, slice metrics, and automated approve/reject decisions.

  • Package the toolchain for on-prem, air-gapped, regulated, or customer-held environments.

  • Close the field-failure loop by feeding live failures back into the next tune cycle.

  • Lead and grow a small specialist team around curation, auto-labeling, deployment, and onboarding.

What success looks like

 

  • Customers can run a full adaptation cycle without engineer intervention.

  • Customer data stays inside the customer boundary.

  • The system produces trusted datasets with clear provenance and quality signals.

  • Pseudo-label quality is measured and systematic errors are caught early.

  • The promotion gate can approve or reject models based on evidence, not intuition.

  • Evaluation is protected by anchor sets, leakage controls, slice metrics, and baseline comparisons.

raw.title: National Retail Account Manager
raw.description:
🛒 Help build ZOE’s physical Retail presence from the ground up.

ZOE has built a world-class personalised health product, and now we’re taking our physical products into retail. We’re looking for a National Retail Account Manager with an FMCG or Consumer Health background to help turn that ambition into reality, owning retailer relationships, product launches, vendor setups, and trading performance that will shape how ZOE shows up on physical shelves.

You’ll have the opportunity to build how we work with retailers from the ground up, sitting within our Supply Chain & Operations team while collaborating across Commercial, Operations, Marketing, and Logistics to make things happen. If you’re commercially minded, operationally sharp, assertive in negotiations, and excited by hands-on retail launch execution, this is your opportunity to have a real impact.

🚀 About the Role

ZOE is entering an exciting phase of growth, and we’re looking for a dedicated National Retail Account Manager to help shape and scale our physical retail channel (across UK grocery, pharmacy, high street, and health & wellness channels) while supporting key commercial partnerships.

This is a highly operational, high-impact role for someone who thrives on turning commercial opportunities into structured launch plans, seamless supply chain coordination, and strong on-shelf execution. You’ll own the day-to-day commercial and operational management of our retail accounts, ensuring launch critical paths are executed across multiple fast-paced launches, retailer portal administration is flawless, trading performance is actively managed, and stock flow is coordinated across the business.

👥 About the Team

You’ll join the Supply Chain team within ZOE’s wider Operations organisation, reporting to the Associate Director of Operations. The team makes sure ZOE’s physical products can be launched, supplied, and scaled reliably. You’ll work closely with Commercial, Finance, Legal, Marketing, Growth, Product, Quality, Customer Operations, Creative, suppliers, warehouses, and logistics providers.

The team is distributed across the UK, EU, and US, working remotely and cross-functionally with a strong focus on reliable execution, clear ownership, and fast problem-solving.

🎯 What You’ll Be Doing

  • Parallel Launch Execution & Onboarding: Own retailer setup, critical path management, and operational readiness from initial account setup through to live trading on shelves. Manage multiple major retail launches running concurrently or in quick succession.

  • Commercial Negotiation & Pushback: Lead commercial preparations and negotiations, owning Joint Business Planning (JBP) inputs, trading terms, operational requirements, and follow-up actions. Confidently negotiate with major UK buyers (e.g., Sainsbury's, Tesco), balancing growth targets with the willingness to push back and challenge terms to protect ZOE's commercial interests.

  • Portal & Product Administration: Coordinate retailer setup requirements, including vendor portals, product information, pricing, pack specs, GS1 barcodes, artwork, product copy, promotional setups, and delivery requirements.

  • Account & Partner Management: Manage day-to-day retail account relationships, ensuring retailer queries, stock blockers, operational decisions, and follow-up actions are handled quickly and clearly.

  • Cross-Functional Driving Force: Act as the central project driver, proactively pulling internal teams (Supply Chain, Ops, Legal, Marketing, Finance) together to resolve blockers, answer operational questions, and keep launch deadlines on track.

  • Trading Performance & Analytics: Track trading performance across sales, rate of sale (ROS), availability, stock cover, promotional uplift, placement, distribution, and retailer reporting, turning data into actionable growth recommendations.

  • Supply Chain & Inventory Management: Support forecasting, purchase order tracking, stock visibility, and service-risk management across current accounts and future retail expansion.

  • Playbook & System Creation: Build repeatable, scalable retail account management processes, templates, metrics, and playbooks from the ground up to support future ZOE expansion across the UK and EU.

🧠 What You’ll Bring

  • UK Retail Market Experience (Must-Have): 2–4+ years of experience in retail key account management, commercial operations, or retail operations within FMCG, CPG, grocery, or consumer health. Proven understanding of the UK retail landscape (e.g., Sainsbury's, Tesco, Waitrose, Boots, Superdrug) is required. Additional international expansion experience is a plus.

  • Ground-Up Execution & Builder Mentality: Hands-on experience taking a product into retail from scratch, with a track record of setting up new internal processes, metrics, and scalable playbooks.

  • Commercial Confidence & Negotiation: Strong commercial acumen with direct experience negotiating with retail buyers. Comfortable advocating for the business, challenging assumptions, and pushing back during negotiations.

  • Retailer System & Portal Fluency: Direct experience managing retailer portals, critical paths, GS1/barcoding standards, artwork sign-offs, and trade term administration.

  • Commercial & Operational Balance: Comfort with forecasting inputs, order and stock tracking, availability metrics, rate of sale, margin structures, and the operational realities of getting physical stock onto shelves.

  • Proactive Stakeholder Leadership: Ability to bring structure to complex cross-functional workstreams, drive alignment across internal teams, and push projects through to completion with high autonomy.

✨ Our Hiring Journey

We value your time. While the exact steps and timeline can vary slightly depending on the role, seniority, and team, we’ve designed a streamlined 4-step blueprint to get us from "Hello" to "Welcome to the team" as efficiently as possible:

  1. 👋 Intro Chat with the Talent Team: A high-energy alignment check to learn about you and share our vision.

  2. 🧠 Hiring Manager Interview: A tactical conversation focused on your craft, experience, and aspirations.

  3. 🔄 The Remote Loop: 2 to 4 focused interviews assessing your technical expertise, behavioural approach, and collaboration style.

  4. 🎉 Offer & Welcome: Finalising the details and getting you ready to hit the ground running!

Once we connect, we pride ourselves on moving fast. Our average hiring process takes between 20 to 30 days, depending on the complexity of the role.

We love momentum, but we’re always happy to adjust the timeline to match your schedule and personal preference.

title: Superviseur·se CVC/HAVC - Pompes à chaleur - France
description: Octopus Energy, fournisseur d’énergie verte présent à l’international, a lancé sa filiale Octopus Energy Services pour accompagner ses clients dans la décarbonation complète de leur foyer. Déjà bien implantée au Royaume-Uni, cette entité propose un ensemble de solutions techniques : installation de panneaux photovoltaïques, de bornes de recharge pour véhicules électriques et de systèmes de chauffage décarboné, le tout avec une approche centrée sur la qualité, l’innovation et la satisfaction client. Et aujourd’hui on a besoin de toi pour propulser notre croissance ! Nous recherchons une personne passionnée, ayant de l’expérience dans l’installation de pompes à chaleur et/ou systèmes de chauffage et désireuse de nous aider à développer cette activité en France. Il s’agit d’un poste sur le terrain couvrant la région d’Amiens, mais tu seras également amené·e à travailler depuis ton domicile ou depuis notre bureau de Lille lorsque cela sera nécessaire. Tu n’as pas peur de partir d'une feuille blanche, tester, apprendre et avancer en autonomie. - Tu es proactif·ve et rigoureux·se , tu sais organiser ton activité en autonomie, en optimisant au fur et à mesure, notamment en mettant en place des processus clairs et automatisés - Tu as l e goût du challenge , tu aimes aller sur le terrain ; tu n'as pas peur de te confronter aux artisans et de les aider à surmonter les irritants rencontrés. Doté·e d'un fort capital sympathie, tu sais fédérer tes interlocuteurs et les faire devenir de véritables ambassadeurs d’Octopus Energy ! Pré-requis & Qualifications - Permis voiture en cours de validité - Diplôme(s) de niveau CAP/BEP, ou VAE de niveau équivalent - Avoir travaillé précédemment dans des entreprises certifiées RGE & Qualibat  - Maîtrise de l’anglais technique à l’écrit & l’oral (niveau B1-B2)  - Habilitation électrique (BR NF C18-510) Ce sera également un plus si : - Tu es à l’aise avec les outils & le numérique, notamment Excel - Tu as de l’expérience avec la partie “électrique” des pompes à chaleur  - Tu possèdes l’habilitation électrique BR Pourquoi tu vas adorer travailler pour nous ? Tu as vu le salaire ou la fourchette prévu·e pour ce poste mais tu aimerais en discuter ? Demande-le nous ! Lors de notre premier contact, c’est un point que nous abordons toujours, car même si nous prenons soin de définir des grilles les plus justes possibles, il nous semble également important de faire correspondre ton expérience au bon salaire. Nous aurons l’occasion de t’en dire plus sur la manière dont nous avons défini le salaire et sur les autres avantages dont tu pourras bénéficier si tu nous rejoins ! Sache enfin que nous pouvons avoir un certain degré de flexibilité, car nous ne voudrions jamais que le salaire soit une raison pour laquelle quelqu’un·e ne postule pas chez Octopus - ce qui est le plus important pour nous est de trouver le bon Octofit ! Certifiée depuis 2024 et 4e en 2025, Octopus Energy France est classée 1ère sur plus de 200 entreprises au classement Great Place to Work 2026 ! Cela reflète bien notre engagement pour un environnement de travail épanouissant ! Nous sommes une organisation où les gens apprennent, décident et construisent plus rapidement. Où ils travaillent de manière autonome, avec des gens extraordinaires, sur des projets qui innovent. Intéressement au capital, flex-office, excellente mutuelle, forfait mobilité douce, prise en charge d’une partie de ton titre de transport au-delà du minimum légal, et même des jours de congés spéciaux pour t’investir dans un projet associatif qui te tient à coeur… Nous voulons que ton investissement soit récompensé par des avantages auxquels tu tiens vraiment ! Chez Octopus, nous cherchons des personnes foncièrement bienveillantes et empathiques. L’égalité des chances nous tient à cœur et nous veillons à offrir un environnement de travail inclusif et équitable. Systemische Zusammenarbeit und Weiterentwicklung: Du arbeitest eng mit Social-, Creator-, Community-, Production- und Paid-Teams zusammen, begleitest relevante Produktionen und Offsites und entwickelst interne Prozesse sowie KI-gestützte Arbeitsweisen weiter. Dafür bringst du Reise- und Terminflexibilität mit. Du hast Erfahrung in der strategischen und kreativen Gesamtverantwortung für anspruchsvolle Kunden-Mandate, Kampagnen oder Markenaufgaben. Du kannst Plattform- und Kanalstrategien entwickeln und mit einer übergreifenden Content-Systematik verbinden. Du präsentierst komplexe Strategien sicher vor Entscheider:innen und auf C-Level und kannst unterschiedliche Stakeholder zu klaren Entscheidungen führen. Du hast ein ausgeprägtes Gespür für Marken, Content, Plattformkultur und gesellschaftliche sowie kulturelle Signale. Du kannst kreative Qualität über Konzept, Briefing, Produktion und finalen Output hinweg sichern und Feedback präzise, konstruktiv und verbindlich formulieren. Du hast Erfahrung darin, Playbooks, Standards oder Leitplanken zu entwickeln und Wissen in Teams wirksam zu vermitteln. So arbeitest du Du denkst strategisch und kreativ zugleich und verlierst dabei weder die Marke noch die Plattform oder die Umsetzbarkeit aus dem Blick. Du triffst Entscheidungen eigenständig, übernimmst Verantwortung und schaffst Orientierung, wenn Anforderungen komplex oder noch nicht vollständig geklärt sind. Du kommunizierst klar, verbindlich und verhandlungssicher auf Deutsch sowie sicher auf Englisch. title: Agentic Compiler Engineer
description: ABOUT KOG Kog builds a co-designed inference stack for real-time AI agents on standard datacenter GPUs, spanning model architecture, inference engine, compilers, and low-level GPU kernels. On the model side, we developed Laneformer 2B and Delayed Tensor Parallelism (DTP), a Transformer architecture that overlaps communication with useful computation and weight streaming. On the systems side, the Kog Inference Engine runs this stack on standard AMD and NVIDIA datacenter GPUs. Kog generates 3,500 tokens/s per request on 8 AMD MI300X GPUs and 2,100 tokens/s per request on 8 NVIDIA H200 GPUs, in FP16 at batch size 1, with quantization and speculative decoding disabled. Our next major project is AGCO, our agentic compiler. AGCO is designed to optimize LLMs across different GPUs and optimization targets, including very fast inference. The team has 10 people, including 9 engineers and researchers and 4 PhDs. Test it at playground.kog.ai. Read the technical details on the Kog Labs blog. WHAT YOU WILL WORK ON You will work directly on AGCO. The goal is to build a system that can explore ways to optimize LLM execution, generate changes, compile them, check correctness, run them on real hardware, measure the results, and use this feedback to guide the next optimization. You will contribute to areas such as: Compiler and IR design for representing and transforming LLM computations. Optimization passes, lowering, and code generation. Search methods for exploring different implementations and execution strategies. Verification and correctness checks for generated changes. GPU execution, profiling, and performance optimization. LLM inference across operators, memory, parallelism, and communication. Optimization loops that connect generated changes to measurements on real GPUs. One direction we are exploring combines an IR, a verifier, a compiler, and a search optimizer. We plan to start with focused problems, build working prototypes, and extend the system from what we learn. Your main area will depend on your experience, skills, and interests. You may focus more on compilers, GPU systems, or LLM inference while working closely with people across the full stack. WHAT WE LOOK FOR We look for engineers with deep technical expertise and original work in at least one area relevant to AGCO. Relevant experience includes: Compiler engineering, including optimization passes, IRs, lowering, code generation, LLVM, or MLIR. GPU programming with CUDA, HIP, Metal, Vulkan, or similar technologies. GPU performance work involving kernels, memory, synchronization, profiling, or hardware behavior. LLM inference engines and performance optimization. Attention, MoE, parallelism, communication, or other systems-level parts of LLM execution. Formal verification, equivalence checking, SAT/SMT, or related methods. Systems that generate, search, test, benchmark, or optimize code automatically. We care about what you personally built and the technical decisions behind it. Strong candidates can explain the problem, their approach, the alternatives they explored, and how they measured the result. We review technical work during the process. This can be public code, an upstream contribution, a paper, a thesis, a technical project, or a detailed write-up based on work you can share. WHAT WE OFFER You will join a small team building AGCO as a core part of Kog's technology. Work at the intersection of compilers, GPU systems, and LLM inference. Direct access to engineers working across the full inference stack. A fast loop from an optimization idea to compilation, execution, verification, and measurement on real GPUs. The opportunity to go deep in your strongest technical area while expanding into the other parts of the stack. High ownership over technical decisions and systems that will shape how Kog optimizes LLM inference. This role is based in Paris, and we are looking for candidates who can relocate to Paris and work closely with the team. Find Jobs in France on Arbeitnow

description: We believe conversations will become the #1 way to shop. Our mission is to turn every interaction between a brand and its customers into a relationship: personal, seamless, and intelligent. By combining deep product expertise with the latest in AI, we’re making shopping feel more natural, human, and connected than ever before. You’re motivated by impact, love solving customer problems, and bring structure and curiosity to everything you do. Specifically, you have: 2 to 3 years of experience in a closing sales role (Account Executive or Account Manager) within SaaS or eCommerce tech. A proven track record of hitting and exceeding quota in a fast-paced, high-volume environment. Strong ability to manage a high volume of accounts, balancing multiple deals simultaneously while staying organized and efficient. A knack for asking strategic, pain-based questions that uncover new opportunities and deepen customer value. A data-driven mindset. You use numbers to identify trends, spot upsell potential, and measure performance. Able to juggle for speed and deal velocity, you can move quickly from demo to close while maintaining consultative quality. Excellent time management and prioritization skills; you know how to balance calls, sequences, and follow-ups. Tech-savvy and naturally curious, able to act as a solutions consultant who speaks confidently about how Gorgias drives customer experience and revenue impact. Strong communication skills with clear, engaging, and persuasive communication across written, verbal, and presentation formats. Nice to Have Experience working directly with eCommerce merchants or within a tech startup. Background in running or advising online stores/brands on best practices. Role description

As Senior Project Manager, you will join our central Project Management team in Reinbek, which leads the company's large and complex cross-functional projects and sets the standards for how projects are run across all of arethia's global locations. Join us during a pivotal growth phase and help create the foundations of a team that will drive meaningful transformation across the organisation.

You will independently lead complex projects with senior stakeholders across departments, and you will be the person we turn to when a project has drifted off course and needs to be brought back on track. 

This is a delivery role first, and it is also a chance to shape how project management works in a growing, international company: you will contribute to our standards and methods, support colleagues who run their own projects and help build a project management community across our sites. As the team grows, so does the scope of what you can take on.


Your Mission

  • Project Leadership – Lead large, cross-functional projects independently from initiation to closure, including planning, governance, steering committees and stakeholder management.
  • Problem Solving - Facilitate and actively participate in problem-solving sessions to drive project success 
  • Project Recovery – Take over projects that have drifted off course or lost their lead, diagnose what went wrong and re-establish structure as interim or permanent lead.
  • Stakeholder Management – Navigate demanding situations with senior leadership and across departments and prepare well-founded decisions for steering committees.
  • Quality and Coaching – Support department-led projects as quality assurance and sparring partner and coach project managers on their deliverables.
  • Standards and Methods – Contribute to our project management standards, templates and training formats, and turn project experience into reusable methods.


Minimum Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience.
  • Several years of experience independently leading complex, cross-functional projects with full ownership from initiation to closure.
  • Experience working with senior stakeholders and navigating conflicting interests across departments.
  • Strong analytical and problem solving skills.
  • Experience taking over or stabilising projects already in progress.
  • Ability to work independently, propose solutions and make decisions within your remit.
  • Business-level communication skills in German and English (C1).
  • Experience in applying common project management tools, e.g. for task and milestone tracking.


Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with an ERP or comparable large-scale system implementation.
  • IPMA Level C or equivalent. A higher level is a plus.
  • Experience in a manufacturing or regulated production environment.
  • Experience developing project management standards, templates or training formats.
  • Experience with Jira and Confluence.
  • Experience working in an international, multi-site organisation.


Why you'll love working here

  • Exciting tasks in an internationally operating, growing family business with flat hierarchies
  • Flexible working hours and a hybrid working model
  • 4 weeks remote work from other EU countries
  • 30 days paid vacation per year
  • Salary bands for a fair corporate culture
  • Monthly allowance of €50 for your BAV
  • Annual 360° feedback loops with clear promotion criteria and an individual career path
  • Responsibility from day one in a company that encourages personal responsibility and growth
  • Relocation costs can be reimbursed on a pro rata basis
  • Regular company events such as summer party, Christmas party
  • Paid team dinners or activities for each team twice a year
  • Free parking right outside the door
  • Perks and benefits: JobRad, subsidized lunch, subsidy for the Deutschlandticket, free language courses and discounted memberships at several gyms and for the Wellpass
  • Fresh fruit, free drinks and snacks in the office

Garantir le respect des procédures internes, des normes de qualité et des meilleures pratiques de l'industrie. Contribuer aux améliorations de processus, aux initiatives de formation et à la gestion des écarts. Formation Titulaire d'une licence ou équivalent en Technologie de Radiologie Médicale, Génie Biomédical, Sciences de la Vie ou un domaine scientifique connexe. Compétences Connaissance des modalités d'imagerie médicale et des flux de travail d'imagerie. Compréhension des normes de qualité en matière de soins de santé et des environnements de soins aux patients. Familiarité avec les Bonnes Pratiques Cliniques (BPC) est un plus. Compétences organisationnelles et de communication solides. Capacité à travailler en collaboration au sein d'équipes multidisciplinaires et internationales. Maîtrise professionnelle du français ; l'anglais est fortement souhaité. raw.description:
About Alta Ares


Alta Ares is an air defense Neoprime. We build AI-guided interceptors to counter drones and cruise missiles, along with the software platform that powers them.

Our customers are NATO-aligned militaries and defense institutions, and our systems are regularly deployed during live exercises and operational demonstrations across Europe, the Middle East, and Asia.

Founded in 2024, we have grown to 90 people, raised over $60M, and increased revenue 40× this year. We are now entering a new phase of international expansion, industrial scaling, fundraising, and product development.

Role & Mission

  • Turn radar sensing requirements into FPGA designs that support reliable drone detection in operational conditions.

  • Define how radar data is acquired, processed, and delivered to the rest of the system, working across RF, electronics, and software teams.

  • Establish processing budgets and select implementation approaches based on detection performance, latency, numerical accuracy, and available FPGA resources.

  • Develop reference models to study radar behavior in noise and clutter and guide hardware design decisions.

  • Build reusable RTL functions for waveform generation and receive processing in FMCW and pulsed radar systems.

  • Implement the processing stages needed to extract targets from radar returns, including matched filtering, pulse compression, range-Doppler processing, clutter rejection, and CFAR detection.

  • Integrate ADC/DAC interfaces, coordinate transmit and receive timing, and ensure synchronization with the radar front end.

  • Specify how detections and associated measurements are passed to tracking functions and embedded software.

  • Verify designs against reference models through automated testbenches and hardware-in-the-loop testing.

  • Investigate performance gaps on target hardware and use laboratory measurements and field results to improve the processing chain.

  • Document design decisions, interfaces, and validation results to support integration and future product development.


Candidate Profile

  • At least three years of FPGA development experience, with practical exposure to radar or sonar processing.

  • Ability to take a signal-processing function from an algorithmic description to verified RTL in VHDL or Verilog/SystemVerilog.

  • Strong DSP foundations, including FFT, digital filtering, windowing, and the effects of quantization and fixed-point precision.

  • Understanding of how radar systems estimate target range and velocity, distinguish returns from clutter, and set detection thresholds.

  • Working knowledge of matched filtering, pulse compression, range-Doppler maps, and CFAR techniques.

  • Familiarity with FMCW and pulsed radar, including the relationship between waveform choices, acquisition timing, and digital processing.

  • Experience assessing radar performance through simulation, including signal-to-noise ratio and clutter effects.

  • Experience developing testbenches, debugging FPGA hardware, and validating processing chains with hardware-in-the-loop methods.

  • Master’s degree or equivalent in Electrical Engineering, Signal Processing, Applied Physics, or a related field.

Skills & Qualities

  • Hands-on engineer motivated by making radar processing work reliably on physical hardware.

  • Able to connect system-level performance issues with their causes in algorithms, RTL, interfaces, or timing.

  • Methodical approach to debugging, verification, and documenting technical decisions.

  • Comfortable owning development tasks and coordinating integration work across disciplines.

  • Clear communicator who makes trade-offs explicit and flags risks early.

  • Entrepreneurial mindset with the ability to operate autonomously in a fast-growing company.

  • High integrity and professionalism in handling sensitive defense technologies.

description: About Mistral Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms. We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited. About the job Mistral AI is looking for a Domain Expert in crashworthiness simulations to help build AI-accelerated simulation capabilities for industrial engineering. You will work at the intersection of industrial simulation, physics modeling, machine learning, and engineering workflows. Your role is to bring deep solid-mechanics expertise into the design, training, evaluation, and deployment of AI Physics Models for real engineering use cases. This is a hands-on technical role. We are looking for someone who understands industrial structural simulation not only conceptually, but through direct experience with simulation models, solver workflows, data generation, validation, and engineering decision-making. You will work with research, product, and customer-facing teams to ensure that our models are useful against real engineering standards — not only benchmark metrics. Relevant application areas may include automotive crashworthiness, aerospace structures, consumer-electronics drop/reliability, manufacturing, durability/fatigue, and other nonlinear structural mechanics problems. What you will do Work with our research team to define, generate, and iteratively improve simulation datasets for training and evaluating crashworthiness foundation models, balancing coverage of relevant physical scenarios, simulation fidelity, and computational cost. Design and run high-fidelity simulation campaigns using structural mechanics solvers such as Abaqus, LS-DYNA, Ansys Mechanical, Radioss or equivalent tools. Define the relevant variation space for training data: geometry, mesh resolution, material behavior, boundary conditions, loading, contact, joints, failure modes, and engineering KPIs. Build or guide automated pipelines for simulation setup, execution, post-processing, dataset creation, and model evaluation. Work with research teams to train and evaluate AI models on simulation data, and diagnose failure modes caused by data gaps, poor coverage, numerical artifacts, or model limitations. Evaluate model outputs against industrial engineering needs, including field-level accuracy, scalar KPIs, deformation modes, load paths, energy absorption, stress/strain fields, failure indicators, uncertainty, and out-of-domain behavior. Work with industrial customers to understand their simulation workflows and engineering priorities, define use cases and success criteria, and incorporate their feedback into model development and validation. About you You have deep expertise in crashworthiness, solid mechanics, and structural mechanics, with substantial experience in industrial simulation workflows. You have a Master’s degree or equivalent technical depth in mechanical engineering, aerospace engineering, civil/structural engineering, computational mechanics, applied physics, or a related field. You have 4+ years of relevant industrial experience (or PhD +1 years) in domains such as automotive, aerospace, and consumer electronics. You have hands-on experience with explicit dynamics for crash or impact simulation and understand nonlinear FEM and related topics such as contact, plasticity, structural dynamics, buckling, material modeling, fracture/damage, fatigue, crashworthiness, or durability. You have direct experience with simulation validation, correlation, model quality, numerical sensitivity, and engineering KPI definition. You are a strong Python developer who can build and maintain reliable tools for simulation automation, data processing, and model evaluation. You apply sound software engineering practices, including version control with Git, automated testing, code review, and clear documentation. You have hands-on experience working in Linux and HPC environments, including submitting and monitoring batch jobs, selecting appropriate compute resources, and troubleshooting simulation workflows. You can run simulation campaigns efficiently across a compute cluster. You are comfortable operating in ambiguous technical environments and turning poorly defined industrial problems into scoped datasets, experiments, metrics, and execution plans. You communicate clearly with both deep technical experts and non-specialist stakeholders. It would be great if you Have experience applying machine learning, surrogate modeling, reduced-order modeling, optimization, or data-driven methods to simulation problems. Have contributed to reusable internal tools, open-source code, simulation automation frameworks, or production-quality engineering workflows. Have experience working directly with industrial customers, product teams, or engineering decision-makers. Have publications, patents, internal technical leadership, or recognized contributions in engineering, simulation, computational mechanics, or ML-for-physics communities. You will join our Integrated Photonics team, working across Massy and Palaiseau at the interface between PIC design, characterization, packaging and system integration.

We are looking for a hands-on Photonic Packaging Engineer to take ownership of our packaging activities, improve existing processes and help make our PIC integration more reliable and reproducible.

Your first priority will be to contribute to ongoing packaging activities, develop and improve assembly processes, and troubleshoot integration challenges alongside our PIC design and characterization teams.

As you grow into the role, you will also have the opportunity to develop new packaging approaches, coordinate technical projects and contribute to building more structured and scalable packaging capabilities.

Today, packaging activities involve several members of our team. Having a dedicated engineer will help us accelerate ongoing developments, improve the reproducibility of our processes and strengthen the connection between PIC design, characterization and system integration.

As our PIC platforms evolve, your work will also contribute to developing new integration approaches and preparing our packaging processes for future scale-up.

• Take ownership of ongoing packaging activities and improve existing processes.
• Develop optical coupling, precision alignment and fiber-array attachment methods.
• Work on component assembly, bonding and electrical interconnections.
• Address mechanical and thermal integration challenges.
• Test new approaches, troubleshoot issues and improve process reproducibility.

Qualify and improve packaged devices:

• Build and test prototypes to validate packaging approaches.

• Troubleshoot optical, electrical and mechanical integration issues.
• Establish repeatable procedures and technical documentation.

• Work closely with PIC Designers to anticipate packaging constraints.
• Translate assembly challenges into practical design-for-packaging guidelines.
• Collaborate with characterization and system-integration teams to improve packaged device performance.

Build the packaging capability:

• Collaborate with external packaging partners and equipment suppliers.
• Improve existing equipment, assembly methods and internal capabilities.
• Explore new packaging technologies and integration approaches.
• Support automation to improve accuracy, reproducibility and throughput.
• Progressively lead technical projects and contribute to future scale-up.

How you'll grow:

0–3 months → Get familiar with our PIC platforms, existing packaging processes and integration challenges. Contribute to ongoing activities and start taking ownership of selected technical tasks.

3–6 months → Take increasing responsibility for packaging processes, develop and test improvements, and contribute to making our assembly methods more reliable and reproducible.

6–12 months → Lead packaging development activities within your area of expertise, strengthen our qualification and documentation practices, and contribute to new packaging approaches and technical projects.

raw.title: Network Developer
raw.description:
Senior Network Developer

About Share

Share is the global marketplace for bandwidth. We aggregate telco infrastructure across Africa (fiber routes, subsea capacity, data centers, cloud on-ramps) into a single intelligence layer. That lets ISPs, hyperscalers and AI companies get connectivity where they need it in seconds, not months.

Today, bandwidth is bought and sold through slow, private, one-off deals, with almost no price transparency. We're replacing that with one neutral exchange: an API on top of real infrastructure, with prices set by actual supply and demand. It's already live across East Africa, with thousands of kilometers of fiber, 12 infrastructure providers, 10 data centers, and around 8 million people served.

The Role

Our network is the foundation of the product. Every route a customer provisions through our API has to exist, perform and stay up on real hardware. We're hiring a Senior Network Developer to design and build that network as software: a distributed, multi-provider fabric that engineers change through code, not by logging into devices.

You'll own the network architecture end to end. That covers our BGP edge (transit, peering at KIXP and LINX, private interconnects with hyperscalers), the backbone, and the PoPs and data centers we're adding across the continent. You'll set the standards our network is built to, which partner ISPs connecting to us will inherit. As we grow, you'll also help build the network engineering team.

What you'll do

  • Design the backbone and PoP architecture as standard, repeatable building blocks, from edge to data center, so we can add capacity and new markets without redesigning each time.

  • Drive our move to Segment Routing and a clean IP architecture, including IPv4 reuse, IPv6, and how customer and internal address space coexist.

  • Build on disaggregated white-box hardware (Edgecore with IP Infusion OcNOS today), and make the hardware and software calls that keep us fast and affordable.

  • Turn operations into software. That means a source of truth (Nautobot), templated config (Jinja), and CI/CD with validation, staged rollouts and rollback for every change.

  • Build the telemetry and observability that show what the network is really doing. Use AI where it actually helps: anomaly detection, automated triage, and auto-remediation with a human in the loop.

  • Own availability. Limit how much any failure can affect, mitigate first and diagnose second, and turn post-mortems into fixes in the system.

  • Work with our software team on the API and provisioning layer that exposes the network to customers, and with partner ISPs' engineers on the hand-off.

  • Help hire and develop the engineers who'll run this with you.

Our Ideal Candidate

  • 8+ years building and operating large networks at a hyperscaler, CDN, internet exchange, carrier or ISP.

  • Deep BGP at scale: route policy, communities, RPKI, traffic engineering, peering and transit.

  • Strong data center and backbone design. You know Clos/EVPN-VXLAN fabrics and MPLS or Segment Routing, and when each makes sense.

  • Hands-on with white-box or disaggregated networking, including choosing hardware and knowing where the silicon limits you.

  • You treat the network as code. You write automation yourself (Python or similar), and you've built or run the pipelines, source of truth and telemetry that make that safe.

  • You've owned availability for something that couldn't go down, and can walk us through a real incident: what broke, how you found it, and what you changed.

  • AI-native in how you work. You've built with these tools, not just used them, and you have a view on where they help in operations and where they don't.

  • You think like an owner. You bring ideas, not tickets, and you want to help build a team, not just a network.

  • A clear, direct communicator who's comfortable with partners' engineers and with our founders.

Nice to have

  • Experience at an internet exchange, or running peering at scale.

  • Open networking stacks like SONiC, OcNOS or FRR, or contributions to them.

  • Streaming telemetry (gNMI/gRPC, sFlow), and building your own monitoring tooling.

  • 400G/800G and optical (ZR) deployments, including vendor selection and certification.

  • Access networks (GPON/XGS-PON) and MikroTik or Huawei gear, since many partner ISPs run it.

  • Building networks in emerging markets such as Africa or Latin America.

  • DDoS mitigation at the edge.

If you don't tick every box but have built and run large networks in production, apply anyway.

Compensation & Benefits

Competitive salary and meaningful equity in a venture-backed company (US-incorporated, with a Kenya operating entity)
